title: Compatibility Scorecard and Experimental Soft-Pin Policy for External Open Models
creator: Ayesha Rao
description:
Problem: When we accept community/open models into the Redwood model catalog we currently only record a binary compatibility annotation (compatible / incompatible) and an optional pin. This leads to ad-hoc decisions, unexpected runtime fallbacks, and awkward customer rollouts for models that are mostly compatible but have edge-case behavioral differences.

Goal: Define a repeatable, lightweight compatibility scorecard and an experimental 'soft-pin' policy that gives product, runtime, and customers a clear signal about risk and expected behavior. The scorecard will be mandatory for new external model submissions and will inform automated runtime routing (non-blocking), docs, and onboarding checklists. The soft-pin policy lets us route traffic to a preferred runtime variant while allowing automatic graceful fallback to broadly compatible variants without hard failure.

Scope: This ticket defines the scorecard fields, acceptance criteria, UI annotations required in the catalog entry, runtime routing semantics for soft-pins, customer-facing messaging, and the minimal instrumentation needed to validate the policy during a 4-week experimental rollout. Implementation of runtime routing and automation will be separate ENG tickets (see dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: Define a 7-field compatibility scorecard (format and allowed values) and doc it in Confluence
Scorecard must include: architecture match, tokenizer parity, kv-cache semantics, fp/quantization compatibility, max-sequence behavior, expected sampling determinism, and fallback variant mapping
UI: Catalog entry displays scorecard summary and an explicit 'soft-pin' toggle with tooltip explaining fallback behavior
Runtime: Soft-pin is non-blocking by default - requests are routed to preferred variant but will fall back to compatible variant within 50ms of failed allocation or if latency SLO is breached
E2E tests: Automated test harness that verifies fallback triggers under simulated overload and returns expected variant metadata in tracing headers
Docs: Onboarding doc with decision tree for reviewers and a checklist for maintainers; includes minimum eval prompts to spot common regressions
Observability: Console must show per-model variant error rate, fallback count, and latency delta; create dashboard and alert (P2) for unexpected fallback > 1% of requests in a 24h window
Pilot: Run a 4-week pilot with 3 community-sourced models and capture metrics; post-pilot decision: proceed to full policy or iterate
decisions: Scorecard will be permissive by default (pass/fail replaced with graded signals) to avoid blocking innovative models
Soft-pin routes are advisory: control plane will not automatically change pins without explicit PM/Eng approval
Fallback window (50ms) chosen to balance fast failover and not masking transient issues; actionable if exceeded repeatedly
We will not require existing pinned models to retroactively populate the scorecard during the pilot
notes: Trade-offs: More granular scorecard improves signal but increases reviewer burden. Mitigation: provide defaults and auto-populate fields from runtime probes where possible.
Design: UI copy needs plain-language explanation for 'soft-pin' vs 'hard-pin' to reduce confusion (design will draft microcopy).
Privacy: Scorecard data is metadata only; no model weights or customer data will be stored in Confluence beyond hashes and provenance notes.
open_questions: Which team will own the automated runtime probe that fills 'tokenizer parity' and 'kv-cache semantics' fields? (ENG/infra vs Research)
Should the soft-pin be allowed for Dedicated customers with SLA contracts or blocked by policy?
Do we need a separate 'experimental' catalog tag for soft-pinned models during the 4-week pilot?
What exact tracing header name and schema should runtime include to signal fallback variant?
success_metrics: Pilot coverage: 3 community models onboarded with full scorecards
Fallback rate: fallback triggered intentionally during tests and observed <0.5% in normal traffic
Reviewer effort: average time to review a submission with auto-probes < 45 minutes
Customer clarity: catalog support tickets referencing pin behavior reduced by 30% after UI copy updates
